tickets.short: Codex config parity with Claude Code, one source, self-maintained
tickets.long: Extend the single-source config model in this repo so Codex CLI(codex-cli 0.146.0) reaches parity with Claude Code on every config surface, and a git pull re-syncs both tools via the existing install.sh hooks. Surfaces, per the handoff (.context/attachments/UJfJQs/codex-parity-handoff.md) and the owner's answers of 2026-08-12 (prefix AGNT, remote connector URLs in scope, parity everywhere including agents): (1) MCP(Model Context Protocol) manifest config/mcp-servers.toml plus a Rust tool tools/mcp-sync that writes the mcpServers key in ~/.claude.json and the [mcp_servers.*] tables in ~/.codex/config.toml without touching other keys or tables, backup before write, --dry-run passthrough; includes researched public remote MCP URLs for services now reached only as claude.ai connectors, added where codex mcp login can authenticate them. (2) Global instructions: a repo-tracked file linked to ~/.codex/AGENTS.md carrying the CLAUDE.md substance with Claude-only mechanism references translated. (3) Hook parity: register hooks/rag-recall for Codex's UserPromptSubmit hook with additionalContext injection. (4) Agents fleet parity: the six agents/*.md definitions derived into Codex agent TOML files under ~/.codex/agents/. (5) install.sh gains numbered steps wiring all of the above. Verification per the handoff: section-diff proofs on both live configs, matching mcp list output on both CLIs, and a real Codex session picking up the shared rules.

tickets.short: Spare hand-added servers from state-driven removal
tickets.long:
The state file lists which servers mcp-sync manages. A server on that list, but no longer in the manifest, gets removed from the live configs. A state file that goes false (a hand edit, a bad merge, cross-machine drift) then deletes a server the user added natively.

The fix: store a fingerprint of each rendered server. Before a removal, compare the live entry to the fingerprint. Spare and unlist an entry that no longer matches, and report the spare.

First step, per the owner at gate C: map the consumers of the managed set before the schema changes. Those are the claude and codex removal paths, save_state, check, and adopt. Defer, but not long. Repro: .map/AGNT-0001/scratch/t19-state/repro/a02.

tickets.short: Merge concurrent applies instead of last-writer-wins
tickets.long:
Two mcp-sync applies against the same target at the same moment each write an intact file, and the later rename wins. The earlier change disappears while both runs report success.

The fix is a conflict pass: after a lost race, re-read the target and merge. Prefer to keep both entries and to maximize compatibility.

Low priority: install.sh invokes the tool one run at a time, and the owner runs one agent at a time. The external-writer guard already refuses blind overwrites. Repro: .map/AGNT-0001/scratch/t19b-concurrency.

Trigger note from the close review: install.sh links itself as the post-merge hook, so a git pull inside a live agent session is the likely real-world path to two concurrent applies.

tickets.short: Show remote-server login state per tool
tickets.long:
The manifest adds ten remote MCP(Model Context Protocol) servers, and every one of them needs a one-time OAuth login per tool. No file sync can perform that login.

Add a login-status readout to mcp-sync. It lists, per remote server and per tool, whether authentication exists, so an added-but-not-logged-in server is visible long before it fails at first use. The readout reads each tool auth state and writes nothing.

tickets.short: Gate the rag-recall injection
tickets.long:
The hook injects the top eight chunks on every prompt. Gated retrieval beat that pattern by 2.2 points while it retrieved 70 percent less (TARG). Low-relevance chunks measurably degrade output quality (Chroma context-rot study, 18 models). Stale memories decay into confident wrong answers as the time gap grows.

The fix: inject only when the prompt turns on past work, and otherwise stay silent. The counter-finding sets the bar: a crude keyword gate scored worse than always-on retrieval. The gate must beat that bar, or the hook stays as it is. Anthropic ships the on-demand pattern in its memory tool, which is the fallback shape.

Per the tooling rule, a change to this Python script means a Rust rewrite, never a patch in place. The Codex and Claude registrations both point at the new binary when it lands.

tickets.short: A fast lane in the engineer map for one-sentence diffs
tickets.long:
Planning overhead runs near ten times execution for single-step changes. Anthropic guidance says skip the plan when one sentence states the exact diff. The map today walks every change through all 23 phases.

The counter stays on the record: removing plans cut coding performance 14 percent on 21,120 real trajectories. So the full map stays for real work. The lane covers only the change a single sentence can state, and the owner shapes it at that ticket own gates.

tickets.short: Evaluate research-sweep against the native deep-research workflow
tickets.long:
Claude Code now ships a Dynamic Workflow named deep-research. It fans searches across angles, cross-checks sources, votes per claim, and filters what fails the vote. That is nearly the research-sweep contract.

Run one evaluation: the same goal through both, then compare cited coverage, cost, and the critic value. Retire research-sweep or differentiate it on what the native run cannot do.

tickets.short: Install local and remote tools from one manifest.
tickets.long:
Create one tracked manifest for executable tools. It must accept an embedded repository path or a Git URL and revision. Each entry records supported operating systems, its installer, provided commands, and harness adapters.

Add a Rust sync tool that fetches remote repositories into a managed cache. It must refuse to update a dirty checkout, select the declared revision, run the declared installer, and link each command. Dry run must report every fetch, build, link, harness change, and platform skip without writing.

Keep Model Context Protocol server definitions in config/mcp-servers.toml. The tool manifest references those definitions instead of copying them. Replace the unsupported Pi draft with supported Pi extension or skill paths. Use OwaisQuadri/rag as the first macOS and Linux proof, including a real search through Claude Code, Codex, and Pi.

tickets.short: Manage shell entries and protect generated files.
tickets.long:
Render one managed shell file for Bash and Z shell from the tool manifest. Add cld as claude --dangerously-skip-permissions. Render a managed Secure Shell include for the archlinux Tailscale host, and preserve the user's main Secure Shell config.

Install guards for Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. The guards block direct agent writes to managed configuration fields. Each refusal names the tracked source file or the adopt command. Human edits and unmanaged fields must survive the installer.

Test repeated installs, existing user shell content, direct write attempts, the approved installer path, and dry runs with a temporary home directory.

Amendment (owner, 2026-08-19, AGNT-0014 gate D): the shell prompt shows only the folder name (never full path or user@host); the command-entry line sits on its own row below it, highlighted in a distinct color so command boundaries are clear when scrolling. Also adopt the hand-edited ~/.config/herdr/config.toml (worktree-picker keybinding) under managed config.

tickets.short: Prove tool sync on real Linux.
tickets.long: Run the top-level installer and the network-free tool-sync integration suite on a real Linux runner. Verify dry-run immutability, pinned local Git installation, and repeated installation. Verify command links and Pi extension links without relying only on the platform override. Keep macOS checks active. Publish both results in the repository’s continuous integration output.

tickets.short: Set up missing agent clients.
tickets.long: Detect missing Claude Code, Codex, and Pi commands before adapter configuration. On macOS and Linux, show the supported installation command and require explicit approval before running it. Leave installed clients unchanged. Report clients that the system cannot install. Test detection, refusal, approval, repeated runs, and dry-run behavior with an isolated home and executable search path.

tickets.short: Install the pinned Pi stack with private telemetry.
tickets.long:
Install nicobailon/pi-subagents, Plannotator, HumanLayer show-me, Wayfinder, and grilling from pinned upstream revisions. Keep each upstream checkout unchanged. Add a project-owned Pi extension that records package version, invocation, duration, result status, human correction, and exposed cost fields. Do not record prompts or file contents by default.

Derive Pi-compatible agent metadata from the existing definitions without creating a second prompt source. Disable overlapping bundled agents only after representative project roles pass. Require three reproduced failures with one source-level cause before a fork. Test dry runs, repeated installs, telemetry redaction, and representative agent discovery.

tickets.short: Run Claude Code as a subscription-backed Pi child.
tickets.long: Add a project-owned Pi agent that invokes the installed claude command through the external command runner in nicobailon/pi-subagents. Verify the supported flags from the installed Claude Code command instead of copying an example. Preserve fresh context and worktree isolation for mutation-capable runs. Run one bounded child task and confirm that its result returns to Pi. Verify that the call appears in Claude subscription usage before this route becomes the default.

tickets.short: Create the two-tab Herdr worktree setup.
tickets.long: Install herdr-fresh-worktree from a pinned revision. Add one idempotent, repository-owned Herdr setup for new and opened worktrees. Tab one contains Pi at 75 percent width and a shell at 25 percent. Tab two contains Neovim at 75 percent and a shell at 25 percent. Define event ordering and ownership between herdr-fresh-worktree and hooks/post-checkout before either changes a new worktree. Test repeated setup, dirty destinations, existing tabs, and one temporary worktree.

tickets.short: Show live request and overall diffs in Pi.
tickets.long:
Add one repository-owned Pi extension that captures an immutable Git tree when a user request starts. Refresh the request diff and the overall worktree diff after write-capable tool calls and when the agent settles. Include staged, unstaged, untracked, renamed, and binary files without changing the worktree or its real index. Show compact live status and provide commands for the full request and overall views. Test external edits, empty changes, truncation, binary files, and repositories with an existing dirty worktree.

Amendment (owner, 2026-08-19, AGNT-0014 gate D): selecting a file in the diff view focuses the herdr editor tab and opens that file in nvim (compose with the AGNT-0014 layout: herdr tab focus + pane send/nvim remote).

tickets.short: Add decision aids to the engineering gates.
tickets.long: Add Wayfinder's destination, frontier, fog, and out-of-scope fields to engineering plans. Use grilling only when unresolved answers can change execution. Use show-me for concise system views and Plannotator for visual plan or diff feedback. Keep the existing human gates as the authority and record each aid's output in the run artifacts. Add evaluations that prove the aids do not create new mandatory stops on clean runs.

tickets.short: Restore a Herdr worktree as a replayable cockpit.
tickets.long: Store one repository-owned workspace recipe that restores Herdr tabs, active commands, the selected ticket, the current engineering gate, and live diff state. Restore the child-agent fleet view after a restart. Replace separate setup paths with this inspectable state where the shipped Herdr interfaces support it. Keep secrets and transcript contents out of the recipe. Test a cold restore, a partial existing workspace, stale child state, and repeated restore.

tickets.short: Evaluate the shipped model router, and settle discovery against the static tier file
tickets.long:
RESCOPED 2026-08-20, after a session shipped the thing this ticket said not to build. The original text asked for design only, no runtime code, and model admission through discovered capability, availability, quota, and price rather than a hard-coded list. What landed instead is a working static router: config/model-tiers.json as the one place model ids live, install.sh compiling it into subagents.defaultModel, subagents.agentOverrides and a flat modelTierFallbacks map, tier assignments for 11 agents, a session-level fallback in pi/extensions/usage-limit-continue.ts that walks the tier chain on a usage limit and then resumes on whichever abandoned model returns first, and docs/routing.md as the policy. Treat that as v1 and do not redesign it from scratch.

What remains, in priority order.

1. The evaluation system, which is the half of the original scope nothing has touched. Representative task classes drawn from real dispatches in this repository, fixed inputs, blind grading, repeated trials, uncertainty, model and harness version capture, and content-free result summaries. Two router arms to compare: cheap-first with escalation on a failed check, against predictive tier choice up front.

2. Three findings from the 2026-08-20 session constrain that benchmark, and skipping them repeats the session's mistakes. First, the accept signal cannot be a pass-or-fail gate alone: a free-model run returned the correct answer and still burned 92 seconds, 10 tool calls and 53k tokens, five of them rewriting one file, so a gate-only score keeps it. Count turns and wall-clock beside correctness. Second, the predictive arm must read repository state, not task text: arXiv:2607.00053 reports an information-theoretic error floor for routing agentic work from the task description alone, because a typo and a multi-module refactor read the same. Third, free-tier models failed to terminate cleanly on both observed tool-loop runs, so tool grant shape is a routing variable, not a detail.

3. Do not write the harness from scratch. ulab-uiuc/LLMRouter ships ten router baselines including the cheap-first cascade, lm-sys/RouteLLM scores routers, and FrugalGPT (arXiv:2305.05176) and AutoMix (arXiv:2310.12963) are the published form of the cheap-first arm. Their corpora are one-shot quiz prompts (RouterBench, MMLU, GSM8K, MBPP, MT-Bench) and do not transfer, because the accept signal here is whether a gate passed in this repository. Borrow the method and the metric definitions; write the cases locally.

4. Settle discovery against the static list, on evidence rather than preference. The static file is correct today and the owner's instinct on 2026-08-20 was right that it is hard-coded. The failure it will eventually hit is staleness when a provider ships a model or moves a price, and the cheapest answer is probably a refresh that reconciles config/model-tiers.json against the live registry in ~/.pi/agent/models-store.json, not a capability-discovery engine. Decide with a case where the list actually went stale.

5. Still open from the original scope, and still unbuilt: separating model, provider, account and harness so one model is reachable by any allowed route; covering Codex alongside Claude Code and pi; the quota shadow price that makes a subscription-backed call cost something; a cold-start policy for new models; and an exploration budget that cannot overspend. Each needs a worked example before it earns code.

Acceptance: a benchmark that runs both arms over the local corpus and reports cost per accepted artifact with turns and latency, a decision record naming which arm won and on which task classes, and either a registry-refresh path or a written reason the static file stays hand-edited.

Owner's addition, 2026-08-20: the benchmark should also sweep PER ARTIFACT, not only per router. Run an artifact's own eval cases once on each enabled model and report score beside cost and latency, so the tier assignment for each skill and agent comes from measurement instead of judgment. In his words: "its worth to add a run in each model when running evals for our agent artifacts (ai-author) to see which models are acceptable, which tiers are more efficient for each skill/agent/etc". Build it opt-in, as a --sweep flag on the existing harnesses rather than the default run, because every case times nine enabled models is expensive enough that a default would stop anyone running evals at all. The log-summarizer tiering on 2026-08-20 is the worked example: four runs moved it off T1, and a sweep would have answered that in one command.

Owner's refinement, same day: do not run all nine. Walk UP from the cheapest tier and stop at the first one whose output is acceptable, then record that as the artifact's minimum. In his words: "run it from the bottom up and when output is acceptable then we mark that as the minimum". Two guards, both earned on 2026-08-20. First, one run is a sample of one: the free tier passed a log-summary task and failed the identical task on the next run, so a tier is only accepted after repeat trials clear the threshold, never on a single pass. Second, record the FAILING tier directly below the accepted one, because the boundary is the reusable fact, and it is what makes a re-test cheap when a model or a price moves. Watch for non-monotonicity while doing it: a larger model can fail a format-strict case a smaller one passes, so first-pass-going-up equals the true minimum only once the repeats confirm it. Starting rung is a judgment call, and T2 is the sane default, since T1 failed three of four runs and its failures cost 92 and 150 seconds of latency rather than money. This also turns every metadata.minimum-tier floor into a hypothesis: the four authoring skills carry T4 on judgment alone, and this sweep is what can falsify that.

tickets.short: keep a task's file list true to what the task actually touches
tickets.long: Phase 18's stash content check compares the stashed files against the union of every task's `files` array. On RAG-0001 four files were in the stash that no task claimed: `Cargo.lock`, `.gitignore`, `parity/config.toml` and `src/env_lock.rs`. Two classes of gap produced them. A task that edits `Cargo.toml` generates `Cargo.lock` and never declares it. And a phase-15 fix that CREATES a file never appends it to the owning task, so the file exists with no owner. The check then reads as a possible contaminated stash when it is really an incomplete inventory, which costs a careful reader real time at the one gate where a wrong call is catastrophic. Recorded as D-22. FIX: phase 08 declares generated companions alongside their source, and a phase-15 resolution appends any file it creates to the task it belongs to.

tickets.short: validate a break panel's oracle before trusting its verdicts
tickets.long: A break-panel verdict is only as good as the oracle it is measured against, and nothing in phase 19 checks the oracle. On RAG-0001 the terminal harness used `pyte`, which SILENTLY DISCARDS the rest of a line after U+200D. Every bidi and zero-width-joiner verdict it produced was therefore unsound. It generated a finding that survived TWO rounds and consumed a debugging cycle before round 3 replaced the oracle with tmux and got 77 of 77 agreement with the binary - proving the code had been right the whole time. The failure mode is worse than a missed bug, because it manufactures work and can drive a correct implementation into being changed. FIX: before a harness's verdicts are trusted, run it against a case with a known answer and confirm it agrees. Where an angle depends on a third-party emulator or parser, name it and its version in the report.

tickets.short: assert the ticket counter against the filed ids
tickets.long: `next_nnnn` drifted to one less than it should be on the RAG-0001 run, so the next ticket filed would have collided with an existing id. THE CAUSE WAS NOT THE SKILL: a ticket was filed by hand at gate C, outside phase 22, and phase 22 already states that only its own step may increment the counter. So this ticket is a guard against a rule already being broken, not a missing rule. It is filed anyway because the failure is silent and permanent - a duplicate id cannot be renumbered, since /task-graph refuses renumbering by design - and the check is one line. FIX: assert `next_nnnn == max(NNNN) + 1` on entry to phase 22 and on any roadmap write, and fail loudly.

tickets.short: a canary marker per message to time compaction
tickets.long:
A long session cannot tell when the harness summarized or truncated its context. Compaction timing is therefore a guess. Add a canary marker to each message. A session or a hook then detects context loss the moment the earliest canary disappears. Compaction runs on evidence instead of on feel.

Research the mechanism first: where the marker lives, who checks it, and what the check costs per turn. The user's 2026-08-18 note asks for a canary in each message to time compaction.

tickets.short: start Claude and Codex sessions with a memory search
tickets.long:
The hooks/rag-recall hook injects the top-8 chunks into every Claude Code prompt. Codex sessions have no equivalent, so half of all sessions start without memory. Wire Codex's hook surface to the same rag search --json call and the same injection format. Both harnesses then open with one recall shape.

This ticket refiles cancelled RAG-0031 because its files live in this repo. The user split the roadmaps by repo on 2026-08-18. His words: claude and codex messages should start with searching memories using rag search.

tickets.short: fork show-me into this repo's skills
tickets.long:
The show-me skill runs from a symlink into the tool-sync plugin cache under ~/.cache/tool-sync/humanlayer-skills. A cache re-sync overwrites anything edited there, so the skill cannot hold local changes.

Copy the skill into skills/show-me in this repo. Repoint ~/.claude/skills/show-me at the repo copy through the installer. Record the upstream plugin revision inside the fork. A later maintainer then diffs upstream improvements in deliberately. The user's words, 2026-08-18: clone the skill into the AGNT skills instead of using it from remote.

tickets.short: compact engineering views on the forked show-me
tickets.long:
The RAG-0001 run researched compact engineering views on 2026-08-18 with fifteen cited sources. Build the upgrades on the forked skill. The selection rule: console text first, and HTML only when a diagram family has no terminal story. Class and entity-relationship diagrams stay in that no-terminal family, and sequence and activity diagrams render in text.

Adopt the ascii-dag crate for dependency-graph views. No terminal lane or Gantt renderer exists to adopt. Build that view as a small Rust renderer over tasks.json and measured spans. Keep the agent's payload small and let the renderer draw. A row-per-task data contract costs fewer output tokens than generated markup. The full scan sits in the RAG-0001 run record, exploration.md, agents-repo section.

tickets.short: pr-review skill: a phased review run from the filter output
tickets.long: Author skills/pr-review, a review skill with the same phased intensity as the engineer skill. The run starts from pr-review-filter --json (tools/pr-review-filter, landed with this ticket branch): the inbox group first, then the unclaimed group, in stack order bottom first. Per-repo behavior comes from config/pr-review.toml, which selects the github or graphite platform and the filter defaults. The spine: select one PR, research its context and linked tickets, dispatch fresh-context review agents per dimension (correctness, security, tests, style) per the standing fresh-context review rule, adversarially verify findings, draft the review with severity-ranked comments, hold a human gate before anything posts, then post through gh or the Graphite flow and record the outcome. The skill ships with evals/, logs/, and votes/ per the authoring contract in ai-author.

tickets.short: Auto-continue agents when a usage limit resets (5h/7d)
tickets.long: A Pi extension (pi/extensions/usage-limit-continue.ts) watches after_provider_response for a 429 and message_end for an assistant stopReason="error" whose errorMessage names a usage or rate limit. It resolves a reset instant from response headers (retry-after, *-reset), from reset phrasing in the error text ("resets at", "resets in"), or, failing both, from the 5-hour session window or 7-day weekly window the text names. Local models (ollama/lmstudio/localhost baseUrl) are exempt. On a resolved instant it spawns a detached sleep-then-resume shell job (sleep <wait>, then pi --session <file> --print continue), recorded under ~/.pi/agent/usage-limit-continue/pending.json to avoid a duplicate schedule, and exposes /usage-limit-status. A secondary Rust tool, tools/usage-limit-watch, tails a plain-text log (for headless codex/claude runs whose output is redirected to a file) for the same phrasing and schedules a caller-supplied resume command the same way; it has no access to HTTP headers or model metadata, so a caller passes --local for a log known to be a local model. Both are wired into config/tools.toml and install.sh respectively. Executed directly rather than through the full engineer 23-phase spine, given turn budget; verification: 23 TS unit tests (node --test) and a strict tsc --noEmit pass against both the installed and the latest published @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent types, 7 Rust unit tests plus a real end-to-end run (cargo clippy -D warnings clean), and an install.sh --dry-run/live run against a scratch REPO_TARGET/HOME confirming the new step wires correctly. Not done: an interactive Codex/Claude TUI wrapper (would need PTY passthrough, a materially larger effort) — usage-limit-watch covers only redirected/logged output for those two tools.

tickets.short: statusline extension crashes on stale ctx after session replacement
tickets.long: pi/extensions/statusline.ts render() uses a captured extension ctx after session replacement; ExtensionRunner.assertActive throws (runner.js:360 hasUI -> statusline.ts:212 render, :238 refresh). During AGNT-0014 this killed every pi-subagents workflow wrapper and dumped raw Node stack traces into the Pi TUI (owner screenshots, 2026-08-19). Fix per the runner guidance: never use a captured ctx after newSession/fork/switchSession/reload; move post-replacement work into withSession or re-resolve the ctx per render. Verify by running a workflowScript with two parallel children and confirming the wrapper survives and no trace lands in the TUI.

tickets.short: first-class workspace/worktree palette for herdr
tickets.long: Graduate herdr/worktree-picker.zsh (landed with AGNT-0014: prefix+shift+o popup listing open workspaces to switch, all repos worktrees to open, and known folders as create-ws) into the full palette from the owner gate-UX ask, in his words: search and pick any folder in the filesystem; if a git project, open a worktree or create one (open faster); if not a git project, init a local repo there and open a worktree; search by worktree names; quick switch. Adds create-worktree and git-init-then-open actions to the menu, folder roots configuration, and moves the hand-edited ~/.config/herdr/config.toml keybinding under managed config (with AGNT-0009). Iron-man slot: ship it as a proper herdr plugin action rather than a popup script.

tickets.short: ai-author proposes artifacts from mined session evidence
tickets.long: ai-author decides whether to author only once an authoring job arrives: its own opening section routes what arrived, and the tree answers should-this-exist, never should-anyone-have-noticed. Nothing in the system watches accumulated evidence and proposes a capability unprompted. Mine the evidence that already exists: per-artifact logs/usage.jsonl, run-history.jsonl, and the session transcripts indexed in the personal RAG(Retrieval Augmented Generation) store. Look for a task shape repeated across sessions that the runner currently does inline. Propose a skill by default; propose an agent only on the three grounds that justify one, a different model, a tool grant the runner should not hold, or isolation from a job that spews noise. Guards, both required: the standing answer is zero, per docs/agents-fleet-research.md line 94 (handful, real-writeup ceiling ~5, null hypothesis zero), and every proposal carries the cost it measured rather than a plausible improvement idea, or the section becomes a monthly list that bills a day each and saves nothing. Run it on an interval through the pi-subagents scheduler. Owner asked for this on 2026-08-20, in his words: "it would also be in charge of checking my sessions to find recurring tasks or inneficiencies that could be skills, or subagents if they need a specific agent". Ships as a section inside skills/ai-author/SKILL.md plus eval cases, never as a new sibling artifact, because ai-author rule 1 bans authoring a sibling for a capability an existing artifact owns.

tickets.short: subagent runs drop context.md into the repo root
tickets.long: Every pi-subagents dispatch that leaves the output default alone writes its result to context.md in the repository root and reports it as savedOutputPath. Seen four times in one session on 2026-08-20 (runs 5137e1ca, 8a33cc0c, ef5a3b5b, 721e8478), each leaving an untracked file in a working tree. That is the exact shape the engineer map already bans a phase commit from sweeping up, since widening a commit to git add -A is what put ticket artifacts into a product repo history before. One free-model run rewrote the same context.md five times inside a single dispatch, so the file also churns. Fix at the config layer so the artifact never lands in a project repo: set the subagent output default to false, or point it under the run directory. Gitignoring it is the fallback, not the preference, because it hides the litter instead of stopping it.
